Career Peers

Get career-ready, peer to peer.
Free guidance from fellow Tigers. Schedule a session!

Career Peers seeks to complement the mission of Career Services by connecting students with trained peer mentors who offer free, judgment-free guidance on resumes, interviews, and the job search, so every Tiger can take ownership of their own professional development.

Students

Get free career advising from a fellow Tiger.

Get started!
Future Peers

Apply to join the team and mentor other students.

Faculty & Staff

Bring a Career Peer to your class or student org.

Here's how!
WHAT WE HELP WITH

Everything you need for the next step

Resume & Cover Letter Reviews

Line-by-line feedback that gets your documents noticed by recruiters, not filtered out.

Mock Interviews

Practice the tough questions in a low-stakes room before the real thing.

LinkedIn & Handshake Help

Polish your profile so opportunities come find you too.

Career Fair Prep

Walk in with a plan, a pitch, and the right questions to ask employers.

Elevator Pitch Practice

Say who you are and what you want in under 30 seconds, confidently.

Grad School & Next Steps

Sort out timelines, essays, and whether grad school is even the right move.

HOW IT WORKS

Three steps to more confidence

1

Book a session

Grab a slot through TigerLink, powered by Handshake. No cost, no judgment.

2

Meet your Peer

Sit down with a fellow Tiger who has already been through the job search grind.

3

Walk away ready

Leave with a stronger resume, sharper answers, or a clearer next move.

GOOD TO KNOW

Frequently asked questions

Yes. Every service Career Peers and Career Services offer is free for current UofM students and alumni, no fees, ever.
Appointments generally need about 24 hours notice through TigerLink, powered by Handshake.
A copy of the job posting you are preparing for, or a similar one, so we can tailor the practice to it.
No. Think of Peers as your fast, friendly first stop. Your assigned Career Specialist in your Talent Community handles deeper, individualized guidance.

Want to become a Career Peer?

We look for new Peers each year, students who like helping other students figure this stuff out. Reach out to Career Services to learn what the role involves and how to apply.
